key_insight: AEGIS is a domain-focused benchmark that reveals large gaps in current forensic systems: across seven academic categories and 39 fine-grained subtypes, even top models (e.g., GPT-5.1) achieve only ~48.8% detection and localization remains weak (IoU ~30.09%).
problem_solved: Fills the gap of a comprehensive, domain-specific benchmark for evaluating detection and localization of AI-generated manipulations in academic images, exposing forensic difficulty that generic datasets miss.
method: Curate a large, domain-diverse dataset spanning 7 academic categories and 39 fine-grained subtypes to capture real-world complexity.
Simulate a variety of forgery scenarios (four prevalent forgery types) to stress-test detection and localization, and provide standardized annotations for evaluation.
Run comprehensive evaluations including classification (detection) and pixel/region localization (IoU) across human, baseline, and SOTA model baselines to quantify gaps.
impact: AEGIS gives AI/ML researchers and practitioners a focused, rigorous testbed to benchmark and drive improvements in forensic detection and localization for academic imagery — enabling more reliable integrity checks in scientific publishing and research workflows.
visual_elements: Overview infographic showing 7 categories and 39 subtypes (icon grid) to communicate dataset breadth
Bar chart comparing detection accuracy (e.g., GPT-5.1 ~48.8%) and localization IoU (expert models ~30.09%) across evaluated systems

paper_title: AEGIS: A Holistic Benchmark for Evaluating Forensic Analysis of AI-Generated Academic Images
paper_authors: Bo Zhang, Tzu-Yen Ma, Zichen Tang, Junpeng Ding, Zirui Wang
